verdict.rationale: Sandbox0 documents two timeouts. A soft `ttl` pauses the sandbox on expiry and can be refreshed while work continues, then left to expire when idle. A `hard_ttl` deletes the sandbox's identity and RootFS state. Pricing docs confirm paused sandboxes incur no compute charges, only storage. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration; true activity-based idle detection, since idle shutdown relies on the caller refreshing the soft TTL; and paused sandboxes still accrue storage charges, so billing does not stop entirely unless hard_ttl deletes them.

support.subject: As a developer, I can set timeouts so sandboxes shut down automatically and stop billing when idle or done

citations.quote: ttl: Soft runtime timeout. Expiry requests the same planned pause transaction. hard_ttl: Hard sandbox timeout. Expiry durably requests deletion of identity and RootFS state.
claim a sandbox with a soft ttl; refresh the soft deadline while work continues, then let it expire when idle
On Sandbox0 Cloud, paused sandboxes incur no compute charges.
Paused sandboxes incur storage charges only.
